Illinois Fighting Illini.status: Transfer — from East Carolina, returning to the Big Ten after an earlier spell at Michigan State.
Illinois Fighting Illini.career_experience: Redshirted in 2022 and could not beat out Noah Kim at Michigan State, then started full-time at East Carolina, where he went 13-6 as a starter.
Illinois Fighting Illini.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; the guide records a 13-6 record as an East Carolina starter.
Illinois Fighting Illini.passing: 3,300 yards on 65.9% completions with 19 touchdowns at East Carolina.
Illinois Fighting Illini.rushing: Nine rushing touchdowns at East Carolina.
Illinois Fighting Illini.competition: None described — Houser is presented as the starter.
Illinois Fighting Illini.author_confidence: Cautiously positive. The guide judges he has a better supporting cast in Champaign than he had in East Lansing, while flagging two offsetting factors.
Illinois Fighting Illini.positive_case: A better supporting cast than at Michigan State, following a productive full-time starting season at East Carolina.
Illinois Fighting Illini.concerns: A new system, and an offensive line replacing four starters.
Illinois Fighting Illini.scheme_fit: Flagged as a risk — the guide names the new system as one of two offsetting factors.
Illinois Fighting Illini.supporting_cast: Weak up front. Four offensive line starters leave through graduation or the portal, including first-team All-Big Ten tackle J.C. Davis, and last year's group already struggled to run consistently — Duke, Indiana, Ohio State and Wisconsin averaged five sacks against them. Bielema is content with his backfield, having moved second-leading rusher Kaden Feagin to tight end, and imported only one Power Four transfer, Wisconsin center Jake Renfro.
Illinois Fighting Illini.portal_context: Houser arrives from East Carolina; only one Power Four offensive line transfer was added.
Illinois Fighting Illini.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins. The decisive argument is the schedule and the lines, not the quarterback: three of the last four games are at home but all are coin flips — Nebraska, Iowa and Northwestern — and the guide concludes rebuilding both lines cannot be finished in one season.
Illinois Fighting Illini.outlook_dependency: Moderate. Illinois' 19 wins over two seasons are attributed largely to departed three-year starter Luke Altmyer, so the position matters, but the guide argues its Under from line rebuilding and schedule.

Indiana Hoosiers.status: Transfer — from TCU, replacing Heisman winner and No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza.
Indiana Hoosiers.career_experience: The active FBS passing leader; 19-12 as a productive TCU starter.
Indiana Hoosiers.passing: 9,629 career yards and 71 touchdowns in 36 games and 31 starts.
Indiana Hoosiers.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate; the guide states he can throw.
Indiana Hoosiers.turnovers: 33 turnovers in 36 career games — named as the weakness. The guide argues the environment should fix much of that, noting no FBS team has fewer giveaways over the last two seasons than Indiana's 17.
Indiana Hoosiers.competition: None described — Hoover is presented as the incoming starter.
Indiana Hoosiers.author_confidence: Positive with a named reservation. The guide asks directly whether Hoover can handle it, credits him as productive, and argues the environment mitigates his ball-security record.
Indiana Hoosiers.positive_case: The active FBS passing leader, playing behind what the guide calls arguably the best offensive line in college football, in a programme with the fewest giveaways in FBS over two seasons.
Indiana Hoosiers.concerns: Ball security across his career, and a scheme consequence: Hoover lacks Mendoza's size and athleticism.
Indiana Hoosiers.scheme_fit: Explicitly altered — the guide expects Cignetti and coordinator Mike Shanahan to run less RPO because Hoover lacks Mendoza's size and athleticism.
Indiana Hoosiers.supporting_cast: Arguably the best offensive line in college football, but Indiana loses its top two receivers including first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. and its top two rushers. Talent remains in Charlie Becker and Michigan State transfer Nick Marsh (1,311 yards, nine touchdowns over two years), with Khobie Martin (508 yards, six touchdowns) and Turbo Richard (1,027 yards, 11 touchdowns over two years at Boston College) at running back.
Indiana Hoosiers.portal_context: Cignetti added eight Power Four starters through the portal, Hoover among them. The guide's reservation is cultural as well as talent-based: many departures were the James Madison players who came with Cignetti.
Indiana Hoosiers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 10.5 wins, with the guide explicitly calling 10.5 the right number rather than a mispriced one. Indiana is -350 to return to the playoff and should be favored in every game except Ohio State. A regression argument is offered — Indiana is +37 in turnover margin over two seasons — and the guide's closing view is that going over 10.5 means buying at the top of the market.
Indiana Hoosiers.outlook_dependency: High. The guide's stated regression argument runs through turnovers, and Hoover's 33 giveaways in 36 games are the named risk to a programme record built on ball security.

Iowa Hawkeyes.status: New starter, identity undetermined — the guide states coordinator Tim Lester chooses between two candidates without naming an expected winner.
Iowa Hawkeyes.previous_school: Hank Brown was at Auburn; Jeremy Hecklinski's previous school is not addressed in guide.
Iowa Hawkeyes.career_experience: Hank Brown started one game for Auburn two years ago; Jeremy Hecklinski has two career passing attempts.
Iowa Hawkeyes.previous_starts: Hank Brown one; Jeremy Hecklinski none.
Iowa Hawkeyes.efficiency: Team-level only: Iowa's passing offense has ranked 129th, 130th and 130th nationally in the last three seasons.
Iowa Hawkeyes.competition: Genuinely open and unresolved in the guide. The candidates are Hank Brown, who started one game for Auburn two years ago, and Jeremy Hecklinski, who has two career passing attempts. The guide names no favourite.
Iowa Hawkeyes.backup: The two named candidates are Hank Brown and Jeremy Hecklinski; the guide does not rank them.
Iowa Hawkeyes.author_confidence: Low, expressed as avoidance. The guide sets the bar by the problem — three straight seasons at 129th or 130th nationally in passing offense — and expects Iowa to lean on the run instead.
Iowa Hawkeyes.positive_case: Not addressed in guide for either candidate; the guide's positive case is the run game rather than the quarterback.
Iowa Hawkeyes.concerns: Both candidates are effectively unproven, and Iowa has just lost Mark Gronowski and his 58 career wins after leaning on the portal for starters in recent seasons.
Iowa Hawkeyes.supporting_cast: Strong, and expected to carry the offense: a talented line plus the tandem of Kamari Moulton (878 yards, five touchdowns) and South Dakota transfer L.J. Phillips (1,920 yards, 19 touchdowns in 2025).
Iowa Hawkeyes.portal_context: Iowa responded to replacing 27 seniors, 16 of them starters, with a programme-record 16 transfers — which the guide presents as an acknowledgement that development alone is no longer sufficient.
Iowa Hawkeyes.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, but the guide is candid that 7.5 is the correct number given the questions and that there is little true betting edge. The supporting argument is Ferentz's floor — never fewer than eight wins since 2015 apart from 2020 and 2023 — and the guide gives the staff the benefit of the doubt despite an inexperienced quarterback.
Iowa Hawkeyes.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide names the inexperienced quarterback as a reason for caution but rests its Over on Ferentz's floor and the running game.
Iowa Hawkeyes.conflicts: The guide names two candidates and declines to state an expected starter; this record therefore carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

Maryland Terrapins.status: Returning starter — started as a true freshman in 2025.
Maryland Terrapins.career_experience: True freshman starter in the Big Ten in 2025.
Maryland Terrapins.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Maryland Terrapins.passing: Just under 3,000 passing yards with a 17-to-9 touchdown-to-interception ratio.
Maryland Terrapins.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate; the guide notes he can throw the ball anywhere.
Maryland Terrapins.competition: None described — Washington is the settled starter.
Maryland Terrapins.author_confidence: Positive. The guide credits Washington with about all you could ask of a true freshman starting in the Big Ten and calls him a potential star.
Maryland Terrapins.positive_case: Strong true-freshman production, an offensive line that allowed only nine sacks, and a new coordinator who wants to use his legs more.
Maryland Terrapins.concerns: A receiving corps plagued by drops that needs to become more reliable, and a running game the guide says has been absent for years.
Maryland Terrapins.scheme_fit: Changing and favourable in intent — Pep Hamilton moves to an advisory role and Clint Trickett takes over, wanting more RPO, more designed running from Washington, and increased tempo through more motion and more snaps.
Maryland Terrapins.supporting_cast: Mixed. Four offensive line starters return and the group allowed only nine sacks, but run-blocking is poor: Maryland ranked second-to-last in the Big Ten at 104.3 rushing yards per game, 122nd nationally, with no 1,000-yard rusher since Roman Hemby in 2022. Leading rusher DeJuan Williams (501 yards, three touchdowns) returns and Harry Dalton III transfers in from USC. Maryland returns 71% of its production, second nationally to Notre Dame per ESPN's Bill Connelly.
Maryland Terrapins.portal_context: Harry Dalton III arrives from USC to support Washington and Williams.
Maryland Terrapins.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins, with the guide flagging the price honestly — roughly -170 to -175 is called a juicy amount to lay. The path runs through an opener against Hampton, games at UConn and against Virginia Tech, both with new head coaches, then UCLA, Rutgers, Wisconsin and Purdue away.
Maryland Terrapins.outlook_dependency: High but conditional on others. The guide's conclusion is explicitly conditional: Washington is a potential star, but the group needs more production for him to realize it.

Michigan State Spartans.status: Returning — the incumbent who took over for the final four games of 2025, expected to hold the job.
Michigan State Spartans.career_experience: Took over for the final four games of 2025, going 1-3.
Michigan State Spartans.competition: Live but with an expected winner. Cam Fancher, with 28 starts across Marshall, Florida Atlantic and UCF, will push him, but the guide expects the incumbent to hold the job.
Michigan State Spartans.backup: Cam Fancher, 28 career starts across Marshall, Florida Atlantic and UCF.
Michigan State Spartans.author_confidence: Relatively positive by Michigan State's recent standards. The guide argues the programme should feel better about quarterback than in several seasons, while noting the position has been a revolving door since 2021.
Michigan State Spartans.positive_case: The guide notes two of Milivojevic's three losses came by three points, and observes wryly that he produced a run of backdoor covers against Nebraska, Indiana and Michigan.
Michigan State Spartans.concerns: The position has failed repeatedly since Payton Thorne — neither Katin Houser, Noah Kim nor Aidan Chiles succeeded — and the receiver room has been stripped.
Michigan State Spartans.scheme_fit: New coordinator Nick Sheridan arrives from the same role at Alabama; the guide expects Milivojevic to hold the job for him and Fitzgerald.
Michigan State Spartans.supporting_cast: Thin at receiver. All three top receivers are gone, including Nick Marsh to Indiana. Chrishon McCray (24 catches, 320 yards, two touchdowns) leads the returners but at 5-foot-10 lacks the size of a typical No. 1; KK Smith from Notre Dame and Fred Moore from Michigan were never featured previously. The guide concludes the run game, led by UConn transfer Cam Edwards (1,240 yards in 2025), will have to carry more. Five offensive line transfers arrive with 72 career starts, including FCS Rimington Award winner Trent Fraley.
Michigan State Spartans.portal_context: Fancher, Smith, Moore, Edwards and five offensive linemen with 72 combined career starts all arrived through the portal; the guide stresses this group must gel quickly after 72 sacks allowed over two years.
Michigan State Spartans.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 3.5 wins, and the guide says laying around -150 is worth it. Its stated edge is that the market may be underestimating Fitzgerald as a proven programme builder.
Michigan State Spartans.outlook_dependency: Moderate. Quarterback is named as a reason to feel better, but the guide's edge is the coach and the market's read of him.

Michigan Wolverines.status: Returning starter — started as a freshman in 2025.
Michigan Wolverines.career_experience: Freshman starter in 2025; among the most hyped recruits in Michigan history and the No. 1 overall player in the 2025 class.
Michigan Wolverines.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Michigan Wolverines.passing: 2,429 yards, 11 touchdowns to nine interceptions, 60.3% completions.
Michigan Wolverines.efficiency: 60.3% completions — part of what the guide calls largely underwhelming numbers.
Michigan Wolverines.competition: None described — Underwood is the settled starter.
Michigan Wolverines.author_confidence: Openly unconvinced so far. The guide calls his numbers largely underwhelming and describes him as a quarterback with a lot left to prove, while expecting improvement from coaching alone.
Michigan Wolverines.positive_case: He flashed the form that made him the No. 1 overall player in his class, and the guide expects improvement from coaching alone under new coordinator Jason Beck and quarterbacks coach Koy Detmer.
Michigan Wolverines.concerns: Underwhelming production — 60.3% completions and a near-even touchdown-to-interception ratio — in a season the guide treats as unproven.
Michigan Wolverines.scheme_fit: Explicitly favourable. The guide cites Beck's record — New Mexico's offense went from 44th to fourth nationally in 2024, and Utah's from 115th to fourth last year — and notes the staff wants Underwood running more.
Michigan Wolverines.supporting_cast: Good. Jordan Marshall (932 yards, 10 touchdowns) and five-star freshman Savion Hiter run behind a line returning four starters.
Michigan Wolverines.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins. The guide is explicit that inherited talent is not the problem, resting its case on the schedule and the quarterback: a slate with six ranked opponents and no chance to dodge any of the conference's top teams, a programme still in transition, and a quarterback with a lot left to prove.
Michigan Wolverines.outlook_dependency: Very high. The quarterback is one of the two named pillars of the Under.

Minnesota Golden Gophers.status: Returning starter — started all 13 games as a freshman in 2025.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.career_experience: Redshirt sophomore who started all 13 games as a freshman.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.passing: 63.5% completions for 2,432 yards with 19 touchdowns to six interceptions.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.competition: None described — Lindsey is the settled starter.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.author_confidence: Positive with named limits. The guide says Lindsey has the potential to be special but lacks a true No. 1 receiver.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.positive_case: Solid freshman production across a full season, with Minnesota returning 68% of its 2025 production per ESPN's Bill Connelly and three of the top four pass catchers back.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.concerns: No true No. 1 receiver, with Auburn transfer Perry Thompson the open question, plus doubts on the interior of both lines.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.supporting_cast: The stated constraint. Minnesota ranked 116th nationally on the ground at 3.57 yards per carry and 127th in total offense. Running back Darius Taylor, who has almost 2,500 yards in 28 career games and managed 915 scrimmage yards despite missing five games, turned down portal interest to stay and should be clear of hamstring problems. The line returns three starters and adds Tennessee transfer right tackle Bennett Warren — and the guide concludes Lindsey's progress depends on it.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.portal_context: Auburn transfer Perry Thompson is the open question at receiver; Bennett Warren arrives at right tackle from Tennessee.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 6.5 wins. The schedule offers a break in avoiding Ohio State and Oregon but still requires trips to Indiana, Penn State and Washington. The guide offers a situational path to clearing the number: Minnesota has beaten a ranked opponent as a home underdog in each of the last two years and likely needs the same against Michigan or Iowa.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.outlook_dependency: High, but routed through the line. The guide states directly that Lindsey's progress depends on the offensive line.

Nebraska Cornhuskers.status: Transfer — from UNLV, replacing Dylan Raiola, who transferred to Oregon.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.career_experience: Led UNLV to ten wins and was Mountain West Player of the Year.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.passing: 3,459 passing yards at UNLV, accounting for 33 touchdowns in all.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.rushing: Included in the 33 total touchdowns; the guide does not split the rushing figure out.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.competition: Live, with an expected winner. The guide's own answer to whether there is a true competition is qualified: Colandrea did not transfer in to sit, but TJ Lateef was highly touted, started five games as a true freshman and already knows Dana Holgorsen's Air Raid. It expects Colandrea to win as the more proven commodity.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.backup: TJ Lateef — 904 yards and five touchdown passes, five starts as a true freshman, and already fluent in Holgorsen's Air Raid.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.author_confidence: Moderate, and framed around job security rather than talent. The guide notes Colandrea must meet high expectations to cool Rhule's hot seat.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.positive_case: A Mountain West Player of the Year who led UNLV to ten wins, and the more proven of the two candidates.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.concerns: The stated concern is expectation and context rather than the player — a new defensive scheme, a difficult schedule, and a coach under pressure.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.scheme_fit: Lateef is described as already knowing Dana Holgorsen's Air Raid; the guide does not describe Colandrea's fit to it.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.supporting_cast: Receivers are solid — returning starters Nyziah Hunter (43 catches, 617 yards, five touchdowns) and Jacory Barney Jr (45 catches, 484 yards, five touchdowns), plus Kwazi Gilmer, who started 19 games at UCLA. Running back is a hole: first-team All-American Emmett Johnson (1,451 rushing yards, 15 total touchdowns) was not replaced from the portal, leaving sophomores Mekhi Nelson and Isaiah Mozee. The guide reports Nelson was arrested in late June on an aggravated battery charge, that the charges were dropped, and that his fall camp availability remains undetermined, so true freshman Jamal Rule may be needed early. The line added guards Paul Mubenga (LSU) and Brendan Black (Iowa State) plus tackle Tree Babalade (South Carolina) and must improve on 33 sacks allowed.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.portal_context: Colandrea in from UNLV; Raiola out to Oregon after breaking his leg against USC following a 6-2 start, with uncle Donovan Raiola fired as offensive line coach. Three offensive line transfers added; running back deliberately not addressed through the portal.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 6.5 wins. After three likely home non-conference wins the schedule sharpens in October with playoff teams in consecutive weeks — hosting Indiana then travelling to Oregon — and Ohio State in the home finale. The guide concludes Nebraska looks middling again and Rhule's seat will only get hotter.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.outlook_dependency: High. The guide ties Colandrea's performance directly to whether Rhule's seat cools.

Northwestern Wildcats.status: Transfer — from Michigan State, where he was benched after nine games.
Northwestern Wildcats.previous_school: Michigan State; before that he followed Jonathan Smith from Oregon State.
Northwestern Wildcats.career_experience: 8-12 as a starter across two seasons at Michigan State before being benched after nine games.
Northwestern Wildcats.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; the guide records a 8-12 record across two seasons and a benching after nine games.
Northwestern Wildcats.rushing: Not addressed in guide as production; the guide describes him as the athletic, mobile quarterback Kelly wants.
Northwestern Wildcats.turnovers: Not addressed in guide as a count; accuracy and ball security are named as the risks that could reappear.
Northwestern Wildcats.competition: None described — Chiles is presented as the starter.
Northwestern Wildcats.author_confidence: Guarded. The guide sees a scheme fit while insisting Kelly must also restore his confidence, and closes on accuracy and ball security potentially reappearing as problems.
Northwestern Wildcats.positive_case: A clear scheme fit — he is the athletic, mobile quarterback Chip Kelly wants in a fast no-huddle spread — reunited with quarterbacks coach Jerry Neuheisel, who recruited him out of high school.
Northwestern Wildcats.concerns: Accuracy and ball security potentially reappearing, and confidence needing to be rebuilt after the benching.
Northwestern Wildcats.scheme_fit: Explicitly good. The guide says Kelly finally gives Northwestern a creative offensive mind, and that Chiles is the quarterback type that offense wants.
Northwestern Wildcats.supporting_cast: Solid. A three-pronged run game with Caleb Komolafe (941 yards, 11 touchdowns), gadget back Joseph Hinton (486 yards) and Gavin Sawchuk (486 yards at Florida State); five of the top six pass catchers return including Griffin Wilde (71 catches, 880 yards, eight touchdowns); the line is helped by Jackson Carsello's return at center, letting Ezomo Orotokhai stay at guard, with Grant Seagren arriving at left tackle after 12 starts at Oklahoma State.
Northwestern Wildcats.portal_context: Chiles, Sawchuk and Seagren all arrived through the portal.
Northwestern Wildcats.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins. The guide acknowledges genuine excitement around the new stadium before applying what it calls a dose of reality, and its closing reservations are Chiles' accuracy and ball security potentially reappearing, plus a judgement that the defense can only carry the team so far against this schedule.
Northwestern Wildcats.outlook_dependency: Very high. The quarterback's accuracy and ball security head the guide's list of closing reservations behind the Under.
